items.title: Caixin: "China’s top economic planner is devising an investment and financing mechanism to accelerate the construction of six major infrastructure ne...
items.description_html:
Caixin: "China’s top economic planner is devising an investment and financing mechanism to accelerate the construction of six major infrastructure networks that are projected to attract 25 trillion yuan in investment over the next five years.

The coordinated infrastructure push serves as a crucial countercyclical measure to stimulate demand in the world’s second-largest economy, as fixed-asset investment unexpectedly shrank 6.7% year-on-year in the first seven months of this year."

The projects Caixin discuss were pretty much expected. Beijing has been unable to get consumption growth to accelerate, which means that the only way to keep GDP growth from slowing is to keep overall investment growth from decelerating.

With property investment continuing to decline, and with across-the-board excess capacity (and strained trade surpluses) limiting the ability of manufacturers to increase manufacturing investment, this means, inevitably, that infrastructure investment has to carry the load.

As Caixin carefully notes, the real driver of this investment is not the sudden discovery that China is severely underinvested in certain types of infrastructure, but rather the need to balance the decline in investment elsewhere. It would be a lucky coincidence if this additional investment were actually economically viable.

One, celebrity founders and CEOs often leave behind a leadership vacuum. As the adage goes, nothing grows under a banyan tree. India is witnessing that more frequently as part of the great handover from post-liberalization leaders to the next generation.

And two, the Reserve Bank of India may need to rethink its approach to bank ownership and management. items.title: "The higher-than-expected FCNR++ mobilisation of ~$137bn likely explains why the RBI chose to close the window early. With this, the core banking syst...
items.description_html:
"The higher-than-expected FCNR++ mobilisation of ~$137bn likely explains why the RBI chose to close the window early.

With this, the core banking system liquidity could peak above Rs 10tn in September. With the liquidity impact now larger than anticipated, some durable liquidity-absorption tools are likely to be deployed, including FX shorter tenor sell-buy swaps and MSS, or even ICRR (less likely). They may also be comfortable now taking delivery of their ~$32bn fwd book which is due to maturing in 1 yr, given the liquidity influx. This could naturally take some liquidity pressure off.

That said, it is important to recognise that this represents a future dollar-denominated debt liability, with an indirect fiscal cost through lower RBI dividends -- potentially amounting to Rs1tn+ cumulatively. The funds raised therefore need to be deployed judiciously and productively to mitigate these first-order costs."

- @MadhaviArora7, Chief Economist, @EmkayGlobal

A Difficult Inheritance

In today's India Edition, I examine why HDFC Bank, the country's largest private sector lender, faces its hardest handover yet.

Read about it here 👇 https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-08-31/hdfc-bank-has-to-find-a-ceo-after-jagdishan-and-rebuild-its-board?srnd=undefined

As the hunt for a successor progresses, these events at HDFC Bank confirm two of my worst suspicions.

One, celebrity founders and CEOs often leave behind a leadership vacuum. As the adage goes, nothing grows under a banyan tree. India is witnessing that more frequently as part of the great handover from post-liberalization leaders to the next generation.

And two, the Reserve Bank of India may need to rethink its approach to bank ownership and management. Its tight regulations haven’t always succeeded in keeping bad actors out — think Chanda Kochhar and Rana Kapoor — while its repeated interventions seem to have allowed bank boards to forget that the job of installing capable new leaders is theirs to do.

items.title: RT ClearPath: $QURE uniQure has now submitted both the US BLA for accelerated approval of AMT-130 and the UK MAA on September 2, ahead of the Q3 deadl...
items.description_html:
RT ClearPath
$QURE uniQure has now submitted both the US BLA for accelerated approval of AMT-130 and the UK MAA on September 2, ahead of the Q3 deadline many were focused on. Both applications are supported by the existing 3Y Phase I/II dataset.

As Matt Kapusta put it in the press release:

“The submission of licensing applications… represents an important milestone for the Huntington’s disease community.”

QURE has requested Priority Review. If granted, FDA review would be six months following the 60-day filing review.

And critically, the applications are based on the 3Y dataset. The 4Y analysis is still coming before the end of Q3.

So the upcoming 4Y readout is not required to establish whether QURE can file, that hurdle has already been crossed.

Instead, strong 4Y data could further demonstrate durability just as FDA and MHRA begin reviewing the applications.

items.title: Some trends I have been reading about: 1. Countries like Switzerland have prospered due to their focus on high value add and low volume niche manufact...
items.description_html:
Some trends I have been reading about:

1. Countries like Switzerland have prospered due to their focus on high value add and low volume niche manufacturing goods. Focus on value addition has helped them escape the high volume commoditised industries.

2. Textile exports from India will have a bumper year in FY27. Last years base is a friend due to de stocking and multiple FTAs will contribute to overall growth rates.

3. Peptides are the new growth vector for Pharma Cdmo cos. Margins are higher tides (Peptides+oligonucleotides). Some of the Cdmo companies will surprise big time vs the street estimates. You can read more about it here-

https://soic.substack.com/p/the-peptide-supercycle

4. Memory shortage is here to stay and as per SK Hynix’s CEO, the tight market can last well into 2030s. Nvidias gross profit margin was impacted due to Higher memory prices this Quarter. Look out for optically higher growth for distributors in India and for companies in refurbished laptops.

5. AI trend is here to stay given Nvidia upped its guidance. The next frontier will be the physical manifestation of AI via humanoids. Bearings companies and forging companies will the ones who will be exposed to this optionality. Given humanoids need human joints like dexterity to move and pick up things. Chinese Humanoid games is a must watch to understand this upcoming trend.

6. In some places in the chemical industry. Chinese shutdown again is going to last for multiple years. As the anti involution drive is gathering pace and subsidies have been withdrawn in spaces like xantheine, dyes, pigments & few other bulk chemicals. Even for Amines there is a trend of firm prices post the shutdown in Middle East caused by war.

7. Indian 2W EV adoption is going through an S curve at the moment. Where adoption is exploding+Ecosystem for battery manufacturing for EV & Bess is taking shape in India. This is a space where solar was in 2017-2019. We have to wait for more positive government policies to come here.

8. Software companies in US have started rallying and select few which have far better growth rates in India vs frontline index have started doing well here too. Is the tide turning for good product companies? (just check sales force chart)

9. We are in a world where Europes own decisions like Russian Gas dependence, Over regulation, wage hikes etc have led to de industrialisation. I was speaking to few forging guys from the industry. Multiple plants from Europe are on the blocks due to unviable power costs to do forging and manufacturing. This business is shifting. Let’s see if Indian cos can capitalise on this mega trend.

items.description_html:
RT CSEINDIA
The Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited ( @BPCLimited ) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to collaborate on biofuels, biomass resource utilisation, waste-to-resource solutions and circular economy.

The partnership will explore opportunities across the biofuels value chain, including Compressed Biogas (CBG), with a focus on feedstock assessment and supply chains, biomass and waste management, technology assessment, pilot and demonstration projects, market development, capacity building and knowledge sharing.

It will also look at how biofuel by-products such as Fermented Organic Manure (FOM), digestate, Bio-CO₂ and DDGS  can be put to productive use, as well as exploring carbon-credit opportunities.

Speaking on the occasion, Subhankar Sen, Director (Marketing), BPCL, highlighted the importance of collaboration and partnerships in developing sustainable solutions.

Sunita Narain, Director General, CSE, emphasised the complementary strengths of the two organisations, CSE’s experience of working with municipalities and its understanding of the CBG ecosystem, combined with BPCL’s industrial capabilities and execution strength.

The MoU marks an important step towards bringing together research, policy, waste management and industrial expertise to develop innovative and scalable solutions for India’s transition towards cleaner energy and sustainable resource management.

items.title: Diagnostic index is moving to new all time highs The Four Macro Drivers Behind the Index Rally (as per the Q1FY27 calls of the companies in this space...
items.description_html:
Diagnostic index is moving to new all time highs

The Four Macro Drivers Behind the Index Rally (as per the Q1FY27 calls of the companies in this space)

1) Pricing has rationalized, restoring realizations

> Discounting fatigue is visible across management commentary. Lal PathLabs says there's been "no structural price change" over the last few quarters and pricing is "neither too favorable nor deteriorating".
> Metropolis hasn't taken a single price hike in 18 months (last increase January 2025) yet still grew realizations 5–6% purely from mix, suggesting price competition has stopped eroding revenue.
> Suraksha explicitly avoids deep discounting in its B2C collection centres; Vijaya's last price hike was a limited Hyderabad-only one in June 2025

2) Volume + mix, not price, is the growth engine

> Q1 FY27 volume growth was broad-based: Lal PathLabs patients +8.2%, Metropolis test volumes +11%, Vijaya test volumes +16.5%, Thyrocare pathology volumes +28%, Suraksha tests +11%.
> Wellness and preventive testing is the premiumization lever. Organised players' wellness revenue has grown at ~25% CAGR over 5 years and now contributes roughly 12–25% of revenue. Vijaya's pure wellness mix hit 14.8% vs ~8% pre-COVID; Lal PathLabs' Swasthfit bundle is 27% of revenue growing ~20%.
> Tier 2/3 expansion is the structural volume story. Metropolis believes the small-town healthcare buildout "will continue for the next at least 2 decades". Suraksha and Krsnaa are both expanding aggressively beyond their home markets

3) Operating leverage is restoring margins

> OPMs now span 24.7% (Metropolis) to 42.7% (Vijaya), with the integrated radiology-plus-pathology and B2C-heavy models at the top. Vijaya expanded margins 360 bps YoY on 22.8% revenue growth; Lal PathLabs' OPM hit 31.0% (a four-year-high growth quarter); Suraksha's inflected to ~34.7% as new centres turned profitable.

4) Regulatory tailwind: CGHS/ECHS rate revision

> CGHS (Central Government Health Scheme) rate hikes are adding 2–3% at Lal PathLabs' company level, flowing straight to margin, expected to persist another 2–3 quarters. Suraksha got a ~1.5% top-line benefit; Metropolis barely benefits (~1% CGHS exposure). Krsnaa sees no immediate benefit since tender rates are contractually fixed, but future tenders may reset higher.

items.title: Both Sterlite and HFCL continue to get big orders from MNC's/Hyperscalers. Why are optics replacing copper in DC build out? A few compounding factors ...
items.description_html:
Both Sterlite and HFCL continue to get big orders from MNC's/Hyperscalers.

Why are optics replacing copper in DC build out?

A few compounding factors are pushing optics into places copper used to own in AI data center builds:

Copper hits a physics wall as speeds rise. At today's high per-lane rates, passive copper simply can't span the distances it used to — at 200+ Gb/s per lane, traditional passive copper can no longer span beyond a single server rack, and sometimes not even within a rack. Higher data rates mean more signal loss, more power burned just driving the signal, and more heat. All getting worse as clusters demand faster links.

The traffic problem got much bigger. AI training and inference generate enormous "east-west" traffic — GPU-to-GPU chatter within and across racks — as clusters scale into the hundreds of thousands of accelerators. The primary data-center bottleneck has shifted from transistor performance to interconnect bandwidth and latency, sometimes called the "I/O wall": compute scales through packaging and process tricks, but chip-to-chip I/O doesn't keep pace the same way.

Power efficiency is now existential, not just nice-to-have. In modern AI clusters, moving data can consume up to half of total system energy, and unlike copper, light doesn't suffer from electrical resistance. So, every watt saved on interconnects goes straight back into compute headroom or lower cooling costs, which matters enormously at hyperscaler power budgets.

items.description_html:
RT ishmohit
Some trends I have been reading about:

1. Countries like Switzerland have prospered due to their focus on high value add and low volume niche manufacturing goods. Focus on value addition has helped them escape the high volume commoditised industries.

2. Textile exports from India will have a bumper year in FY27. Last years base is a friend due to de stocking and multiple FTAs will contribute to overall growth rates.

3. Peptides are the new growth vector for Pharma Cdmo cos. Margins are higher tides (Peptides+oligonucleotides). Some of the Cdmo companies will surprise big time vs the street estimates. You can read more about it here-

https://soic.substack.com/p/the-peptide-supercycle

4. Memory shortage is here to stay and as per SK Hynix’s CEO, the tight market can last well into 2030s. Nvidias gross profit margin was impacted due to Higher memory prices this Quarter. Look out for optically higher growth for distributors in India and for companies in refurbished laptops.

5. AI trend is here to stay given Nvidia upped its guidance. The next frontier will be the physical manifestation of AI via humanoids. Bearings companies and forging companies will the ones who will be exposed to this optionality. Given humanoids need human joints like dexterity to move and pick up things. Chinese Humanoid games is a must watch to understand this upcoming trend.

6. In some places in the chemical industry. Chinese shutdown again is going to last for multiple years. As the anti involution drive is gathering pace and subsidies have been withdrawn in spaces like xantheine, dyes, pigments & few other bulk chemicals. Even for Amines there is a trend of firm prices post the shutdown in Middle East caused by war.

7. Indian 2W EV adoption is going through an S curve at the moment. Where adoption is exploding+Ecosystem for battery manufacturing for EV & Bess is taking shape in India. This is a space where solar was in 2017-2019. We have to wait for more positive government policies to come here.

8. Software companies in US have started rallying and select few which have far better growth rates in India vs frontline index have started doing well here too. Is the tide turning for good product companies? (just check sales force chart)

9. We are in a world where Europes own decisions like Russian Gas dependence, Over regulation, wage hikes etc have led to de industrialisation. I was speaking to few forging guys from the industry. Multiple plants from Europe are on the blocks due to unviable power costs to do forging and manufacturing. This business is shifting. Let’s see if Indian cos can capitalise on this mega trend.

New Market Leaders. Buy the relative-strength leaders, not the laggards — the names showing new leadership within their group.

New Institutional Owners. Fresh, high-quality institutional sponsorship coming in & new funds building positions, not stale holders.

New Market Trend. The general market itself turning into a new uptrend (since 3 of 4 stocks follow the market).

items.title: Long time since I posted here. Not because of markets. The technology, the process, and the conversations around both have been moving so fast that I ...
items.description_html:
Long time since I posted here.

Not because of markets. The technology, the process, and the conversations around both have been moving so fast that I had to choose. Focus. Realign. Reskill. Build.

In my line of work, that felt like the only honest move. The last 6–8 months were really hard. Loss of my FIL who was as close to me as my father, markets punishing bullish bets wore down hard.

I love to build. When I do, it helps me heal. Different people, different ways of coping. I was also wrong on some bets, and that stung.

Hard lesson for me: don’t put your neck out for a business or a person you haven’t known long enough. Show conviction in position size, not in posts. I learned that the expensive way.

One of the bigger lessons: the worst mistakes are often made in the best of times.

Looking back over the last two years, most of what I’m paying for today was done during the bullish phase back 2yrs ago. I trusted people. I took management at their word. I didn’t force a third perspective hard enough.

Bullishness clouded judgment on a few fronts. That’s not usually how I operate. This time the reasoning went quiet, and I missed things I should have seen. The intent was never bad. I still hold the positions. What wore me down was the DMs, the name-calling, the cheap shots. I thought I have lost the trust of those who looked up to me. For a while that made posting here feel pointless.

This isn’t the first time I’ve been against the wall. Every time I’ve been pushed into a corner, I’ve come back by doing the work.

The last six months were that: a lot of agentic systems, harnesses, and observability built inside the enterprise. Quiet work. Deeply satisfying. I’ll keep posting the things that matter. There are still enough people here who value the perspective and see beyond stocks and price points. That’s enough for me. I do not seek a reply or a like, just sharing a heartfelt message here. Cheers. Keep building.

items.description_html:
RT Swapnil Srivastav
🚨 Indian logistics companies have found the perfect scam: steal from D2C brands and let the customer take the blame.

Here’s how it works:

→ Prepaid order gets “cancelled” without the customer or brand knowing

→ Brand gets charged two-way delivery fees for an order nobody cancelled

→ Small items get shipped back in oversized boxes to inflate the RTO cost

→ Customer calls in confused: “I never cancelled this, I was waiting for it”

The brand loses the product, the shipping cost, the RTO cost, and the customer relationship. In one transaction.

Every D2C founder in India has lived this. Not once. On repeat.

And the wildest part? This is a multi thousand crore leak across the industry and almost nobody is building to fix it. 🤷🏻‍♂️

items.title: RT Sridhar Vembu: Last week, I was fortunate to visit the workshop (the Tamil word pattarai பட்டறை is so appropriate) of the leading motor desig...
items.description_html:
RT Sridhar Vembu
Last week, I was fortunate to visit the workshop (the Tamil word pattarai பட்டறை is so appropriate) of the leading motor designer in the world Morihiro Saito-san.

Saito-san is 80+ and still designing advanced motors, some of the most advanced in the world. His modest looking workshop is right next door to a company that builds out those motors in prototype quantities and he works closely with them to get them built. I visited as an industrial "pilgrim", with as much devotion as I go to the Thoranamalai Murugan Temple at home. When I saw him at work, I was moved to touch his feet.

Saito-san, the God of motors, is how Japan is able to retain its global prominence in so many foundational industries.

We need to learn from that spirit. We need to revive our "pattarai" culture of building things - every village in India needs such workshops!

My industrial pilgrimage to Japan has given me new vigor 🙏

items.description_html:
This is the site where our new 100 acre Integrated PCB mega campus will be built in 🇮🇳

We have been working hard to fix the structual gaps in PCB manufacturing in 🇮🇳

Some of the problems are harder than we think and it takes time to fix those.
We have been working on fixing all those problems that every single customer has told us over time and we work hard to make sure that each of those are fixed by identifying the root cause.

Our dedicated team of Terra Circuits will be focused on some of these infrastructre related problems.

PCB Fabs- Inspired by the way TI expanded semicon fabs in Dallas, we will be taking a similar approch here. There will be multiple Fab Units that will be built over time in this campus.

PCBA- we will have enough lines to support our customers scaling to larger numbers.

Components warehouse- a fully automated warehouse to ship components the same or next day.

R&D center- to research and build technologies related to manufacturing, not just pcb. Semicon and advanced applied engg.

I am dedicating my next 10 years building this campus and change the way electronics gets manufactured in 🇮🇳

items.description_html:
*India Cables and Wires- Key points from UltraTech press release and Launch event (STRONG NEGATIVE reaction likely in C&W stocks tomorrow)*

Ultra Tech (UTCEM) just put up its press release with launch of wires and cables today with ‘ *Ultravolt* ’. 2 days ago, UTCEM had announced commercial production of Wires & Light Duty Cables.

*Likely C&W stocks reaction:* Negative (UTCEM likely to invest aggressively beyond what was committed earlier as well as very aggressive posturing on marketing/likely pricing).

*Key highlight of press release (link below) from C&W perspective:*

· At launch itself, Ultravolt will be the *second largest player in the wires segment by capacity* (we aren’t sure about this assessment, at present- await clarity)

· Aims to build a scaled national brand and become *one of the top two players within 5 years.* (means it will invest substantial amount of over INR50-60bn-assuming 5-6x asset turn)

· *Plan is to reach more than one lakh retailers* and further activate availability through over 5,000 UltraTech Building Solutions (UBS) outlets. Already tapped 500 districts and 6,000 pin codes, with commitment to growth and innovation.

*Key inputs from the launch event* (as received from our sources):

· Only wires was unveiled today while light duty cables to happen in few weeks. HT cables early next year (implies faster than initial expectations of commissioning)

· Best in class serviceability will be ensured with 20 warehouses- (this will drive increase in inventories for peers as well- to ensure quick turnaround)

· E-beam technology across product categories- (a relatively standard feature now, we believe)

· Strong connect with electricians, consultants, partners and influencers with foreign travels, t shirts etc (relatively standard practice for industry; however, incumbents might have to step up)

· Solid advertisement campaigns across online and off-line (sentimentally negative as optically will appear significant competition)

· While the launch of wires and cables was already expected, the stated intent to become *one of the top-two player within five years* and the *second-largest player in the wires segment by capacity* is something new, in our opinion. We believe this implies likely aggressive pricing approach.

items.title: P/B ratio has historically been a more reliable and stable valuation metric for predicting future returns compared to alternatives such as P/E or EV/E...
items.description_html:
P/B ratio has historically been a more reliable and stable valuation metric for predicting future returns compared to alternatives such as P/E or EV/EBITDA. I had demonstrated this through correlation analysis in an earlier investor memo.

The chart below tracks the P/B ratio (blue line) of the Nifty Smallcap 100 Index against the 25th percentile of its trailing 5-year P/B range (orange line). In simple terms, when the blue line falls below the orange line, the current valuation is in the lowest quartile of the past five years.

Since P/B is broadly proportional to ROE, the structural improvement in index ROE—from ~8–12% in the previous decade to ~15% currently—has led to a gradual upward shift in the orange line over time.

Notably, for the first time since the COVID crash, the current P/B has moved below this 25th percentile threshold. Historically, similar instances—during the 2011–2013 downturn, Q1 2016 correction, and the COVID crash—have been followed by strong returns over the subsequent 1–3 years.

This does not imply that markets have bottomed, nor does it guarantee short-term gains. In an event-driven environment, especially with geopolitical risks such as an escalation in war, markets could decline further by 10–20%.

However, what can be said with a reasonably high degree of confidence is that forward-looking returns over a 1–3 year horizon from such valuation levels have historically been better than average.

items.description_html: In my experience, this is probably the first time the Mid & Small cap indices have outperformed the Nifty 50 during a crisis time. It's also extremely rare to see the Mid & Small cap indices (avg of the two) beating the Nifty 50 near the bottom of the cycle. Their avg CAGR has outperformed during the last two tough years as well as all the below trailing years. I am not that surprised as their balance sheet, P&L and cash flow quality has substantially improved post COVID. I believe the biggest multi-baggers will emerge from this space as the earnings growth differential will be significant going forward. Because of the quality differential today vs during pre-COVID period, I would be surprised if their valuations correct to levels seen during the previous crashes. We probably have the best corporate quality and least stressed financials currently compared to any other previous big crisis.

items.title: As seen in the table from my latest memo, drawdowns in small caps during the January–March period—measured from the January peak to the February/Mar...
items.description_html:
As seen in the table from my latest memo, drawdowns in small caps during the January–March period—measured from the January peak to the February/March trough—are not an exception; they are a recurring feature of market cycles. Just as consistently, these phases have been followed by sharp recoveries once the market establishes a bottom in February or March.
Current sentiment is such that investors are overly focused on the negatives, making the environment appear so foggy that positives have become invisible. This fog, as always, will eventually lift.

While market bottoms and the depth of drawdowns can never be predicted, it is highly probable that market levels a few months from now will be disproportionately higher. Unfortunately, short-term declines are unsettling for investors, causing many to step aside and miss the eventual strong upswing.

In hindsight, this phase will look like an obvious opportunity. But while living through it, investors see only risks and landmines—never the runway for the next flight

items.title: Let's dissect a heart surgery at Narayana Hrudayalaya like it's a manufacturing process—because in many ways, that's exactly what it is. 8:00 AM, NH ...
items.description_html:
Let's dissect a heart surgery at Narayana Hrudayalaya like it's a manufacturing process—because in many ways, that's exactly what it is.

8:00 AM, NH Bangalore. Operating Room 3 is completing its first surgery. OR 4 is midway through. OR 5 is prepping. Dr. Ashwin moves from OR 3 to OR 4 seamlessly. No downtime. No waiting. By 6 PM, he'll have completed eight procedures. At Apollo down the road, their best surgeon might do two.

The math is elegant in its simplicity. Fixed costs—the OR, equipment, overhead—get divided by eight instead of two. The surgeon's salary, among the highest costs, gets allocated across four times the procedures. Suddenly, that $100,000 American surgery can be done profitably for $1,600.

But the real genius isn't in the division—it's in the multiplication. When you do eight surgeries daily, 2,900 annually, patterns emerge that you'd never see doing two daily. Complications become learning opportunities. Variations become data points. Excellence becomes inevitable through repetition.

By combining innovative technology and a highly efficient delivery system, Narayana Health is able to optimize productivity and minimize costs. Let's decode what "innovative" really means here. It's not about buying the latest robotic surgery system—though NH has those too. It's about innovation in process.

Take procurement. When you're using 10,000 stents annually instead of 100, you don't go through distributors. You call the manufacturer's CEO directly. You negotiate prices that would make American hospital administrators weep. A stent that costs $3,000 in the US, NH buys for $300. Same product, same manufacturer, 10x price difference through volume.

The supply chain innovation goes deeper. NH standardizes everything that can be standardized. Instead of surgeons having preferences for 20 different suture types, there are three. Instead of 50 different implant options, there are five. This isn't compromising choice—it's eliminating meaningless variation that adds cost without value.

One of India’s leading manufacturers and exporters of electrical steel laminations, with capacity at six plants across Telangana, Maharashtra, and Karnataka.

That company is Pitti Engineering Ltd - A Hyderabad-based electrical steel lamination manufacturer founded in 1983, and now an integrated platform spanning stamping, machining, casting, and sub-assembly under a single P&L.

items.title: The semiconductor supply chain is crazier than most people realise. A chip isn't just silicon + a fab. A chip can involve 6,000+ suppliers across 40+ ...
items.description_html:
The semiconductor supply chain is crazier than most people realise. A chip isn't just silicon + a fab.

A chip can involve 6,000+ suppliers across 40+ countries.

Some of the companies involved will surprise you -

Japan's TOTO is famous for making toilets. But it also makes highly specialised ceramic electrostatic chucks used inside semiconductor manufacturing equipment.

These ceramic components use electrostatic force to hold silicon wafers precisely in place during manufacturing.

Then there is Ajinomoto. Yes, the company famous for MSG. It makes Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) — a critical insulating material used in semiconductor package substrates underneath high-performance CPUs and other advanced chips.

Ajinomoto says ABF has a ~95% share in its relevant high-performance application.

Just absolutely crazy!

A toilet company helps hold wafers while chips are manufactured.

An MSG company makes material underneath some of the world's most advanced processors.

Semiconductors are truly crazy, unbelievable and truly global!

In August 2026, electric two-wheelers (EV 2W) accounted for 10.5% of total two-wheeler registrations in India, according to Vahan data compiled by industry analysts

EV 4-wheeler sales inflection point is 5% of sales; in June 2026, we were at around 4.5%

Jan–Aug 2026 penetration is already 6.2%, versus 4.3% for CY2025, with 212,191 registrations in eight months — already exceeding the 195,802 EVs registered in the whole of 2025

All over the world, where EV sales have reached 5% of total sales, EV adoption has picked up really quickly

By 2023, 31 countries had crossed 5%, and Bloomberg's analysis found that some markets subsequently went from 5% to 25% in under four years.

Once millions of vehicles get onto the road, several things start reinforcing each other:

More EVs → more chargers → better economics for chargers → less range anxiety → more EV buyers → more models → OEM scale → lower costs → better resale ecosystem → more buyers.

That's the positive feedback loop.

BloombergNEF's Corey Cantor described this phenomenon essentially as a “virtuous cycle"!

items.title: Making money and creating wealth are two very different things. You can make money from a trade, a good year, a bonus, a business deal or even luck. B...
items.description_html:
Making money and creating wealth are two very different things.

You can make money from a trade, a good year, a bonus, a business deal or even luck.

But wealth is built differently.

Wealth is what remains after years of earning, saving, investing, making mistakes, surviving bad markets and allowing compounding to do its job.

Making money requires skill.

Creating wealth requires skill + discipline + patience + temperament.

Money can be made quickly.

Wealth usually cannot.

Perhaps that's why making money is exciting, but creating wealth is boring.

And boring, done consistently for decades, can become extraordinary.

The event brought together industry leaders, entrepreneurs, civic representatives and policymakers to discuss how Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar can unlock its next phase of growth.

items.title: RT Sanjay Srivastava: National security meets startup capitalism on the ISM 2.0 highway. How does India balance sovereign IP control with the global v...
items.description_html:
RT Sanjay Srivastava
National security meets startup capitalism on the ISM 2.0 highway.

How does India balance sovereign IP control with the global venture capital needed to scale its hi-tech ecosystem? 𓇲⚖️💰

The policy dilemma, frictions, and solutions:

1. The Setup:
* Target: Mission-critical silicon across defence, telecom, and critical infrastructure.
* The Sweetener: 9% Design-Linked Incentive (DLI) on net sales for 5 years, with no upper ceiling.
* The Catch: Mandatory IP co-ownership with @CDACIndia to ensure national tech sovereignty.

2. The Friction:
* VC Hesitation: Global venture capital avoids state-co-owned IP; clean cap tables and unencumbered assets are standard.

* Global Lock-out: Geographic IP restrictions risk cutting Indian startups off from global supply chains, cross-border M&A, and licensing.

* Supply-Heavy: Subsidises production without creating domestic demand-side pull or solving high testing/capex barriers.

3. The Way Forward:
* Flexible Licensing: Shift from rigid co-ownership to non-exclusive licensing or security-compliance frameworks.

* Ease IP Borders: Relax geographic export barriers so startups can access global markets and foreign capital.

* Demand Guarantees: Back DLI with assured public procurement in domestic telecom and energy grids.

* Shared Labs: Subsidise centralised testing and verification infrastructure to slash early-stage capex.

Balancing strategic security with market scale will decide if India builds isolated design hubs or global semiconductor giants.
@AshwiniVaishnaw
@SemiconIndia

By @SurakshaPinnuET & @Subhayan_ET

@pranaykotas & #CounterpointResearch

#Semiconductors #IndiaSemiconductorMission #MakeInIndia #DeepTech #VentureCapital

items.title: RT Prasanna Viswanathan: This is a good oped in Sunday Times. India has already created 12 million gig jobs without a government jobs guarantee, giant...
items.description_html:
RT Prasanna Viswanathan
This is a good oped in Sunday Times.

India has already created 12 million gig jobs without a government jobs guarantee, giant factories or taxpayer-funded payrolls. That is something to build on not something to be ashamed of. And for many, platform work is not exploitation but a dignified escape from low-productivity, low-paying alternatives.

Wage dynamics are revealing. A garment worker in a formal factory earns roughly ₹12,800 to ₹15,700 a month across Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Gujarat and Haryana. OTOH,a platform driver can gross around ₹27,000, or roughly ₹19,000 after operating costs while retaining something a conventional factory job cannot offer.+ flexibility and the ability to enter the labour market almost immediately.

And the oped also points to the ideological contradiction of whose who have disdain only for 'gig jobs

These are same folks who celebrate MNREGA as dignified employment somehow regard a person freely choosing to deliver food, drive a cab or take platform work as being “exploited”.

MNREGA can pay as little as ₹252–₹336 a day in the states Yet the same people who defend guaranteed state-funded manual labour often want to regulate away flexible market-based work that workers themselves choose.

Protect workers with accident insurance, portable social security and transparent algorithms. And fight mindset regulating an imperfect but rapidly expanding source of opportunity out of existence.

India: Bumper finale to the FCNR(B) scheme

1⃣ RBI’s FCNR(B) 2026 scheme garnered a staggering $127.2 bn in inflows vs Nomura’s $80-90 bn estimate. Flows nearly doubled in the final 10 days, taking inflows to 3.1% of GDP vs 1.4% in 2013.

2⃣ Nomura sees BoP surplus rising to $66 bn in FY27 from a $23.6 bn deficit in FY26.

3⃣ But the big question now: How does RBI mop up the surplus liquidity? VRRR operations, an incremental CRR hike, and sell-buy swaps could all be on the table.

Bumper FX inflow is welcome but managing the liquidity aftermath is the next challenge.

items.title: The fear on the FCNR in my view is primarily about inflation. When you add some 9 lakh crore plus in rupee liquidity by printing rupees, especially at...
items.description_html:
The fear on the FCNR in my view is primarily about inflation. When you add some 9 lakh crore plus in rupee liquidity by printing rupees, especially at a time of high credit growth, there is the fear that secondary inflation rises. Usually this happens with a bit of a lag, 6m to 18m.

RBI needs to reduce the liquidity thus created, otherwise it will have to raise rates. The Balance sheet of the RBI was already bloated, and it will bloat even more now.

items.title: I agree, I don't understand the issue against manufacturing or chip making. It is when you make that you accidently or pointedly discover what more ca...
items.description_html:
I agree, I don't understand the issue against manufacturing or chip making. It is when you make that you accidently or pointedly discover what more can be made. Just moving defence imports to local manufacturing helped us make much more in drone and other equipment.

We already have people that can design chips. Then make them too, it's a leap that's taken much capital in the past and for the first time we have adequate domestic capital.

We need to make things. Not import 95% of our umbrellas. Or all our sewing machines. Just reducing imports by making more means so much more.

We need to explore our oil reserves. Our gold reserves. Make thorium work for us. Change energy to mostly self sourced, make things for India and so on.

We do need to reduce red tape and allow for more labour reform, etc. And cut corruption much more.


Prasanna Viswanathan: Long interview. Besides his usual tirade against industrial policy, which by now sounds increasingly hollow, Raghuram Rajan's reasoning for criticising India’s semiconductor mission is particularly bizarre.

Chips, he argues, are “the most easily smuggled thing on earth.”

items.title: RT Ajay Rotti: So the third member passed an independent order. The order at the end said "The matter be placed before the Original Division Bench for...
items.description_html:
RT Ajay Rotti
So the third member passed an independent order. The order at the end said "The matter be placed before the Original Division Bench for passing appropriate orders in terms of the majority opinion under Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, 2013".

Someone read it as being the majority opinion. We had all the outrage that we had. Then the Original Bench says... the third member disagreed with both the Member Technical and Member Judicial. So there is no majority view.

Now, we have a 5 member Bench which will hear afresh and I also understand that the Third Member order has been stayed by the 5-member Bench now!

All the outrage for nothing. For an order which wasnt even an order 😂

This is Indian litigation AND business news reporting at it's finest. Absolute finest.

India’s energy transition is no longer just about adding renewable capacity, it is about building an ecosystem that can deliver energy security, reliability and sustainable growth.

At #CareEdgeConversations, industry leaders Mr Kuldeep Jain, Founder & MD, @CleanMax_Ofc; Mr Sandeep Lakhanpal, Managing Director, @JHargrett49946; Mr Kailash Vaswani, CFO, ReNew Energy Global PLCC; and Mr Abishek Pareek, CFO, Waaree Group came together to discuss what lies ahead for India’s energy transition.

Moderated by Sachin Gupta, ED and CRO, CareEdge Ratings, the conversation highlighted some of the critical priorities shaping the next phase:

🔹 Transmission infrastructure needs to keep pace with the rapid addition of renewable capacity.

🔹 Renewables + storage are increasingly becoming commercially competitive with conventional power.

🔹 Supply-chain resilience and backward integration will be critical to India’s energy security.

🔹 Domestic solar manufacturing has significant potential, but scale, technology, and cost competitiveness remain key.

🔹 Capital availability remains strong, particularly for robust projects, while access to debt needs continued attention.

🔹 The C&I renewable energy segment is witnessing rapid growth, opening up significant opportunities for developers.

🔹 Ultimately, India's transition will require an integrated ecosystem spanning generation, transmission, storage, manufacturing, and finance.

The message was clear: India’s renewable journey is entering a more complex but significantly larger phase, one where energy transition and energy security must move together.

items.title: RT Gregory Brew: With benefit of hindsight, it does appear as though Iran was pushing its luck back in July, when it resumed attacks on shipping in th...
items.description_html:
RT Gregory Brew
With benefit of hindsight, it does appear as though Iran was pushing its luck back in July, when it resumed attacks on shipping in the southern route.

The Iranian calculation was that it was necessary to maintain effective control over Hormuz flows.

The result: the MOU is dead, the blockade is back in place, and the US is succeeding (to a partial, but notable extent) at reopening the strait without another deal.

Perhaps the status quo swings back in Iran's favor, but right now this looks like a miscalculation to me.


Gregory Brew: Agree

Iran is pushing its luck in Hormuz--there's clearly a belief that US is deterred, that Trump doesn't want to go back to war, and there's scope for continuing the war-time use of force to govern flows through the strait.

US response is very clear: bombings will continue

رئيس مجلس الوزراء وزير الخارجية @MBA_AlThani_ يجتمع مع وزير الخارجية الإيراني

طهران | 27 أغسطس 2026

اجتمع معالي الشيخ محمد بن عبدالرحمن بن جاسم آل ثاني، رئيس مجلس الوزراء وزير الخارجية، اليوم في طهران، مع سعادة السيد عباس عراقجي، وزير الخارجية بالجمهورية الإسلامية الإيرانية.

جرى خلال الاجتماع، استعراض آخر تطورات الأوضاع في المنطقة، والجهود المبذولة لخفض التصعيد وتهيئة الظروف الملائمة للحوار، بما يسهم في تعزيز الأمن والاستقرار الإقليميين.

كما تطرق الاجتماع إلى المناقشات الجارية بشأن الإطار المرحلي المقترح، الذي يتضمن إنشاء ممر ملاحي مؤقت مشترك عبر مضيق هرمز، والاتفاق على تنفيذ مشروع مشترك لتطهير المضيق من الألغام.

وشدد معالي رئيس مجلس الوزراء وزير الخارجية، خلال الاجتماع، على ضرورة احترام سيادة دول الجوار، واحترام حرية الملاحة، مؤكداً أهمية مواصلة الجهود الدبلوماسية لخفض التصعيد ومعالجة الخلافات عبر الحوار.

من جانبه، أعرب سعادة وزير الخارجية الإيراني عن شكره وتقديره لدولة قطر على استمرار مساعيها وجهودها الدبلوماسية الرامية إلى خفض التصعيد ودعم الحوار.

items.title: AI and software stocks are now rising together. The 1-month correlation between AI-related stocks and software stocks has risen +0.70 over the last mo...
items.description_html:
AI and software stocks are now rising together.

The 1-month correlation between AI-related stocks and software stocks has risen +0.70 over the last month, to +0.15, marking its largest monthly increase since July 2025.

By comparison, the 1-month correlation was as low as -0.56 in July 2026, as investors increasingly viewed AI as a threat to traditional software businesses.

As a result, hedge fund exposure to software and services stocks declined -5 percentage points over the 12 months ending July, to just ~1% of total global hedge fund market exposure, near its lowest level on record.

The recent increase in correlation comes as some software firms previously viewed as vulnerable to AI are actually finding ways to use the technology to strengthen their existing businesses, improve productivity, and defend their competitive advantages.

Meanwhile, the US software ETF, $IGV, is up +39% since its April low, recovering most of its drawdown that began in October 2025.

The AI trade may be shifting from disruption to adaptation.

items.title: The diesel market is facing a major supply shortage. The US diesel refining margin is up to a record $106/barrel, surpassing $100 for the first time. ...
items.description_html:
The diesel market is facing a major supply shortage.

The US diesel refining margin is up to a record $106/barrel, surpassing $100 for the first time.

This is a key measure of how much refiners can potentially earn from turning a barrel of crude oil into diesel, with wider margins signaling tighter diesel supplies and higher refining profits.

Diesel refining margins have more than tripled since February.

By comparison, during the 2022 energy crisis, this metric peaked at ~$85/barrel.

The surge reflects a severe shortage of global diesel supplies amid the Iran War.

As a result, US diesel inventories are down to 103.4 million barrels, their lowest on record for this time of year, while retail diesel prices are up to $5.78 per gallon, just 4 cents from their all-time high set in June 2022.

The global fuel shortage is becoming far more severe than the crude oil market alone suggests.

This metric has surged +16 percentage points since Q1 2025.

By comparison, the 2022 peak was ~77%, while the 12-month average is ~37%.

However, this percentage remains significantly above the ~32% average seen in the 20 years before the 2020 pandemic.

To put this into perspective, during the 2012-2019 period, this figure never materially exceeded 30%.

The fight against inflation is far from over.

items.description_html:
History suggests volatility is ahead.

Since 1928, the S&P 500 has fallen ~55% of the time in September, making it the only month of the year when negative returns have occurred more often than positive returns.

Over this period, the average return of the index has been -1.1%, with an average drawdown of -4.7%.

Furthermore, the best September recorded a +14.4% gain, while the worst saw a -29.9% decline.

The weakness has historically been concentrated later in the month, with the second half of September averaging a -0.9% return, making it the weakest 2-week period of the year.

By comparison, the first half has seen an average decline of -0.2%.

September has historically been a weak month for US stocks.

items.title: RT Prabhu, CEO, Fibocan: Re Thank you Prashant. Please stress this point if are in any high level meeting with SEBI and other stakeholders 1. Expiring...
items.description_html:
RT Prabhu, CEO, Fibocan
Re Thank you Prashant. Please stress this point if are in any high level meeting with SEBI and other stakeholders

1. Expiring day F&O traders should be settled at 15.15 price ( no need to build any additional 30 minutes vWAP for managing it. Jus the simple LTP (Last traded price) can be used as a reference price for settling options 2. Living or open F&O contracts can be allowed to trade between 15.20 till 15.40 as the case is now 3. To make CAS a realistic Equilibrium price discovery mechanism, the CAS price cannot be more than + or - 0.30% ( Yes less than half a percent) from the 15.15 traded price. This will ensure there is no undue manipulation and hence less of volatility 4. Manage by Exceptions - In the rarest of rare cases ( ie when "Unknown Unknown Risk" where there is some major news flow that has come in which has the potential to impact the price, then SEBI can direct exchanges open another window between 15.30 to 15.33 where the price movement can be allowed by another 2% on either side. If still the news is such a breaking one ( like announcement of lock down), another 3 minute window can be allowed, where in normal circuit breaker can be introduced ( whatever circuit level currently set in) 5. Please note that this exception is like Emergency exit and should be triggered only on the "Rarest of the Rare Cases" ( occurrence of Unknown Unknown Risk situation) only

items.title: RT Nimesh Shah: CITI On RBL Buy, TP Rs 440 RBL has capitalized on its promoter’s Emirates NBD relationship to unlock a disproportionately large pool ...
items.description_html:
RT Nimesh Shah
CITI On RBL
Buy, TP Rs 440
RBL has capitalized on its promoter’s Emirates NBD relationship to unlock a disproportionately large pool of FCNR (B) deposits from the UAE corridor, mobilizing gross FCNR(B) deposits of US$3.4bn (Rs324.72bn) under RBI swap facility.
This is an outsized haul for a mid-sized bank, representing 26% of total deposits, 37% of term deposits, & 2.7% market share in FCNR(B) mobilization – a remarkable feat, dwarfing Bank's >0.5% systemic deposit share. Earnings implications are consequential.
Accretion translates into a tangible ~7% uplift in absolute NII & 10% in PPOP (FY27); however, expanded balance sheet denominator & structurally thin incremental NIMs on FCNR flows will exert optical NIM pressure of 40-45bps over next two quarters – partial drag in 2Q; full impact in 3Q.
This will be partially cushioned by NIM accretion flowing from Rs260bn equity infusion.
Ultimately, NIM trajectory will be governed by deployment timing and utilization of unleveraged deposits.
@CNBCTV18Live @_RituSingh @latha_venkatesh

items.title: Ather Energy: Building A Scalable EV Platform Beyond Premium Scooters Ather is transitioning from a premium electric scooter maker into a broader EV m...
items.description_html:
Ather Energy: Building A Scalable EV Platform Beyond Premium Scooters

Ather is transitioning from a premium electric scooter maker into a broader EV mobility platform by expanding its product portfolio, manufacturing capacity, distribution network and software ecosystem.

Key Strategic Progress

1. Product Portfolio Expansion

Expanded beyond the core 450 platform with Rizta S (159 km) and Rizta S (161 km) variants.
Rizta has become Ather’s fastest-selling product, strengthening its presence in the family scooter segment.
Upcoming EL platform and e-bike portfolio could expand its addressable market beyond scooters.

2. Geographic Expansion

Replicated its South India success model in new markets.
Middle India market share increased from 4.1% in Q1 FY25 to 17.4% in Q4 FY26.
The company is now scaling this playbook across the rest of India through stronger retail and service presence.

3. Distribution & Service Network Scale-Up

Retail and service network doubled during FY26.
Wider footprint improves customer accessibility and supports faster adoption in new regions.

Higher operating leverage

Scale benefits

Investment Perspective
Ather’s next phase is not just about selling more scooters — it is about building a vertically integrated EV ecosystem.

Expansion beyond South India

Improvement in margins

items.title: Ashutosh Fibre IPO : A Technical Yarn Player Moving Towards Higher-Value Products Ashutosh Fibre is an interesting play on technical textiles rather t...
items.description_html:
Ashutosh Fibre IPO : A Technical Yarn Player Moving Towards Higher-Value Products

Ashutosh Fibre is an interesting play on technical textiles rather than conventional textile demand. The company manufactures specialised yarns engineered for specific performance characteristics such as high tensile strength, flame resistance, heat resistance, chemical stability, abrasion resistance and anti-static properties.

Its products ultimately find applications across defence, protective clothing, automotive components, filtration and pollution control, geotextiles, industrial fabrics, thermal insulation, packaging and home furnishing.

Why the Business Looks Interesting

1. The biggest change is happening in the revenue mix and profitability.

Revenue from operations increased only modestly from Rs. 109.9 crore in FY24 to Rs. 117.4 crore in FY26, but EBITDA increased from Rs. 16.1 crore to Rs. 31.1 crore over the same period.

As a result:

EBITDA margin: 14.7% → 15.6% → 26.5%
PAT: Rs. 7.0 crore → Rs. 8.5 crore → Rs. 16.0 crore
PAT margin: 6.4% → 7.5% → 13.7%
ROCE: 21.0% → 16.3% → 26.3%

So FY26 growth was less about topline acceleration and more about a sharp improvement in business mix and profitability.

The most interesting development is the shift away from Indutech towards higher-growth categories.

2. What Industries Does It Serve?

Its yarn portfolio gives it exposure to several specialised applications:

Protech: Flame-retardant and heat-resistant yarns used in PPE, safety apparel and industrial thermal barriers.

Mobiltech: Friction-resistant yarns used in brake pads, clutch facings and transmission components.

Indutech: Filtration, filter cartridges, ropes, webbings and other industrial applications.

Hometech: Home furnishing textiles, carpets and filtration media.

Its broader product range includes para-aramid-based spun yarn, high-tenacity polyester, meta-aramid, FR viscose, modacrylic yarn, polypropylene yarn, stainless-steel yarn and specialised friction-spun yarns.
That creates exposure to structural themes including industrial safety, defence, automotive, pollution control and filtration, infrastructure and specialised manufacturing.

3. Capacity Is Becoming The Next Constraint

The company's main technical/synthetic yarn capacity stood at 3,750 MT in FY26, while production reached 3,619 MT.

That means utilisation has increased sharply:

FY24: 80.2%
FY25: 86.6%
FY26: 96.5%

This is important because the existing facility is approaching full utilisation precisely when newer categories such as Protech are scaling.

Ashutosh Fibre therefore plans to expand within its existing Petlad, Gujarat facility, adding compact spinning systems and high-value yarn attachments such as the Pinter Hard Core system.

Expanding within the existing facility should allow the company to leverage existing infrastructure, workforce and administrative resources — potentially making the expansion more capital-efficient.
Moving Downstream Into Modacrylic Fabrics
Another interesting strategy is forward integration.

4. Moving up in Value Chain
Ashutosh already manufactures modacrylic-based yarn used for high-performance fabrics. It now wants to move into manufacturing and selling the fabric itself.

The company has started trial production through third-party weaving and processing facilities and is targeting approximately 20,000 metres of modacrylic-based fabric sales per month.

The important part is that Ashutosh's own yarn would be consumed as the raw material.

This potentially allows it to move from being only a yarn supplier towards a higher-value finished technical textile product, improving value addition and potentially margins.

5. Exports Could Become Another Growth Lever

Exports are already meaningful:

FY24: Rs. 47.9 crore — 43.6% of revenue
FY25: Rs. 43.4 crore — 38.1%
FY26: Rs. 45.8 crore — 39.0%

The company plans to use additional capacity to target new international markets for specialised technical yarns.

Ashutosh Fibre is interesting because three transitions are happening simultaneously:

Volume → Value: Higher-value technical and performance yarns are becoming more important.

Yarn → Fabric: The company is attempting to move downstream into modacrylic technical fabrics.

Domestic + Existing Exports → Larger Global Opportunity: Nearly 40% of revenue already comes from exports, while new capacity is intended partly to deepen international penetration.

IPO coming at 12.5 PE

items.description_html:
Gaja Capital is raising funds through an IPO primarily to meet its own sponsor commitments in its AIF structures, including offshore vehicles.

A key question is — if the existing sponsor capital has already increased by nearly 20% in the last year, why does the company need to raise fresh capital from public investors to invest further in these high-risk, illiquid assets?

Interestingly, around 85% of Gaja’s income comes from management fees and carried interest, while income from sponsor commitments contributes only about 10%.

This raises a fundamental question: a significant portion of the fresh issue proceeds is being deployed toward an activity that currently contributes a relatively small share of revenue.

Moreover, carried interest is dependent on successful exits and realisation of investment gains. Until portfolio investments are monetised, the carried interest recorded in financial statements may not necessarily translate into actual cash inflows.

The key investor question is whether the additional sponsor commitments will create enough incremental value through future fee income and carry generation to justify the capital being raised

items.description_html:
🚨 C2C’s auditor has issued a qualified opinion and flagged multiple serious financial and compliance concerns:

1️⃣ Liquidity & Going Concern Risk:
The company is facing a liquidity crisis, with statutory dues unpaid due to lack of funds. Recovery from trade receivables remains uncertain, while operations are heavily dependent on short-term promoter funding. The auditor has raised doubt over C2C’s ability to continue as a going concern. Liquidation Risk

2️⃣ CSR Payments Not Cleared:
CSR expenses were recognised through cheques, creating a book overdraft. However, the cheques were not presented for payment. The auditor noted that the CSR obligation is discharged only when the payment is actually cleared.

3️⃣ Statutory Dues Pending:
Undisputed statutory payments remain unpaid. No provision has been made for possible interest or penalties. Delays in filing statutory returns and weak internal controls were also highlighted.

4️⃣ Labour Code Impact Not Assessed:
The company has not quantified the potential impact of new labour regulations on gratuity, provident fund, wages and other employee benefits.

5️⃣ FEMA Compliance Issues:
Overseas receivables remain unrealised beyond RBI timelines. Applications for regularisation are pending, SOFTEX registration is yet to be approved, and possible penalties have not been provided for.

items.title: Supriya Lifescience - FY26 Annual Report Analysis Supriya Lifescience is a niche pharmaceutical company engaged in developing & manufacturing Active P...
items.description_html:
Supriya Lifescience - FY26 Annual Report Analysis

Supriya Lifescience is a niche pharmaceutical company engaged in developing & manufacturing Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API), finished dosage formulations & CMO/CDMO solutions. The company supplies more than 40 specialised APIs to over 1,500 customers across 120+ countries.

The company has historically operated as an API manufacturer but is gradually evolving into an integrated life sciences platform. Its next phase involves expanding into finished formulations, developing new niche APIs & undertaking long term contract manufacturing programmes for global pharmaceutical & innovator companies.

The business is highly export oriented, with international markets contributing 82% of FY26 REV. Europe is the largest geography with a 40% share, followed by Asia at 33%, Latin America at 20%, North America at 3% & other markets at 4%.

Backward integration is central to Supriya’s business model. Backward integrated products contributed 76% of FY26 REV.

The model also gives Supriya greater flexibility while negotiating long term contracts with global customers. Customers in regulated markets value consistency, traceability & supply security alongside pricing, making backward integration an important competitive advantage.

Supriya has a portfolio of more than 40 APIs, including 15 backward integrated products. Its major therapeutic categories include anaesthetics, antihistamines, analgesics, vitamins, anti-asthmatics, anti-allergics, antihypertensives & other specialised products.

Anaesthetics are the largest therapeutic category, contributing 54% of REV. Management is addressing this by launching products across cardiovascular, ADHD, liquid anaesthetics & other niche therapeutic segments.

Newer products started contributing meaningfully during FY26. A cardiovascular product launched during Q3FY26 has begun scaling with a strong order pipeline, while the ADHD portfolio witnessed encouraging demand across Europe & Latin America.

The company also commercialised a liquid anaesthetic API & began regular supplies during the year. Four new APIs were successfully developed & commercialised. Management intends to commercialise three to four new products annually.

CMO/CDMO is emerging as an important long term growth engine. Instead of manufacturing only its own APIs, Supriya is increasingly working with pharmaceutical companies to develop & manufacture products under dedicated or exclusive arrangements.

The company is evaluating exclusive manufacturing opportunities in liquid inhalation products, GLP-1 development & supply for an Indian generics company. Multiple finished dosage development & supply opportunities are also under consideration.

Supriya is expanding beyond APIs into finished dosage formulations through its Ambernath facility. The formulation platform is developing products across tablets, capsules, injections, nasal sprays and liquid inhalation products.

The company commissioned a dedicated production block for a CMO customer & installed a precision distillation facility for a strategic API supporting long term contract manufacturing opportunities.

Planning has commenced for two additional manufacturing blocks at Lote. These investments will support new products, higher volumes & additional CMO/CDMO opportunities.

The Ambernath facility expands Supriya’s capabilities beyond APIs into formulation development & manufacturing. The company is also developing a new industrial site at Isambe, Patalganga, which can provide capacity for the next phase of growth.

Supriya operates three R&D centres - two focused on APIs & one on formulations. It employs around 90 scientists across API & formulation process development.

Supriya is increasing its participation in regulated markets such as Europe, the US & Japan. The unannounced USFDA inspection of the Lote facility in February 2026 concluded with one minor observation, which was subsequently addressed. The company also holds approvals or certifications from EDQM, Health Canada, WHO-GMP and other regulatory bodies.

Growth drivers
- The first growth driver is the scale up of newly commercialised APIs across cardiovascular, ADHD & liquid anaesthetic categories.
- The second driver is the launch of three to four new products annually, which should progressively diversify the product portfolio & reduce dependence on legacy molecules.
- The third driver is regulated market penetration.
- The fourth driver is CMO/CDMO opportunity
- The fifth driver is forward integration into formulations. Successful commercialisation can expand Supriya’s addressable market & increase its share of the pharmaceutical value chain.
- The sixth driver is capacity expansion across Lote, Ambernath & Patalganga.

FY27 outlook : Management remains committed to achieving the 1,000 Cr REV milestone in FY27 while maintaining a healthy EBITDA margin.

Growth is expected to be supported by higher capacity utilisation, the scale-up of recently commercialised APIs, increasing regulated market penetration & a growing contribution from CMO/CDMO projects.

items.title: Milky Mist - Q1FY27 Key Insights Milky Mist started FY27 on a very strong note, with Q1 REV growing 44% YoY to 973 Cr. Gross profit stood at 332 Cr wi...
items.description_html:
Milky Mist - Q1FY27 Key Insights

Milky Mist started FY27 on a very strong note, with Q1 REV growing 44% YoY to 973 Cr. Gross profit stood at 332 Cr with margin expanding around 270 bps to 34.2%, while EBITDA grew 75% at 145 Cr.

The important part is that growth was broad based across categories.

Paneer remains the core of the business and contributed 27% of Q1 REV at 248 Cr, with REV growing 34%. Cheese grew 38%, Curd 27%, while Ice Cream REV increased 60% with volumes up 45%. Yogurt was another standout category which grew 145%.

The structural opportunity in Paneer looks particularly interesting.

Management: "...the pricing difference between the organized and unorganized players has become almost nil."

GST on Paneer becoming zero has reduced the pricing disadvantage that organised manufacturers historically faced. At the same time, regulatory action against analogue Paneer is helping accelerate the shift towards branded players.

Management: "...we don't sell pouch milk. So we are only into a value added product category."

This is probably one of the biggest differentiators versus many traditional dairy companies. Milky Mist operates across 20+ VADP categories.

Milk procurement remains the largest raw material cost, accounting for around 50-55% of total input costs. Management indicated that it still has the ability to take further price increases if sustained procurement inflation begins putting pressure on margins.

The next major structural growth opportunity is Protein.

Milky Mist already sells High Protein Paneer, High Protein Cheese, Greek Yogurt & Skyr & management says the Protein portfolio is among the fastest growing & higher margin parts of the business.

Today, whey generated during Paneer & Cheese manufacturing is largely sold as a B2B by product. Milky Mist is investing in a Whey Protein Concentrate facility that should allow it to convert this stream into significantly higher value B2B & potentially B2C protein products. Management expects the facility to become operational in roughly 15-18 months & believes it can contribute to both REV & margin expansion.

Milky Mist commissioned a new Natural Cheddar Cheese plant during Q1 with capacity of around 120 MT/day. The company is simultaneously expanding capacity across Whey Protein Concentrate, Yogurt, Cream Cheese, Natural Cheese & Processed Cheese.

Management indicated that scale itself can contribute roughly 50 bps of margin benefit, while additional upside can come from better capacity utilisation & better product mix. Management did not formally guide towards 17-18% EBITDA margins, but clearly said that there is meaningful headroom for margin expansion over the next 3-4 years as utilisation improves.

South India currently contributes 69% of REV, while Non South contributes around 31%. Importantly, South itself grew around 44% YoY while Non South grew around 50%. Management believes the mix could gradually move towards around 60:40 over time.

The cold chain infrastructure matters because many VADPs require chilled or frozen distribution. Every new VisiCooler/freezer effectively expands the number of outlets capable of carrying categories such as Yogurt, Ice Cream & other chilled products.

The company operates across 22 states & 5 UTs with 4,200+ distributors, around 375 primary transportation vehicles, 600+ secondary vehicles and more than 41,000 VisiCoolers/freezers at retail outlets. It plans to deploy another 50,000+ coolers/freezers over the next 3 fiscal years.

items.description_html:
Indian dairy market is expected to grow from Rs 12 trn in FY26 to 19.6 trn by FY31P, implying ~10% CAGR

VADPs (Value Added Dairy Products) are growing faster than milk. Milk is expected to grow at ~8% CAGR during FY26-31P, while Traditional VADPs are expected to grow at ~12% & Emerging VADPs at ~15%.

The market mix is steadily shifting towards VADPs. Milk's share declines from 49% in FY26 to 44% by FY31P, while Traditional VADPs increase from 47% to 51% & Emerging VADPs from 4% to 5%.

Organized penetration in paneer is still just 5%, leaving significant headroom for branded players to gain share, expected to grow 20% CAGR.

Other high growth categories include khoa at ~26% CAGR, buttermilk & lassi at ~23%, curd at ~19%, cheese at ~18% & flavoured/frozen yogurt at ~17%

Longer shelf life + rising health awareness + increasing protein consumption + convenience + higher disposable incomes + shift towards branded packaged alternatives are the key growth drivers

items.description_html:
RT Moses Harding John
Re The contribution of new generation private banks (since 1994) is significant to the Indian Banking sector & extended further to holistic BFSI coverage from early 2004!

What went wrong?

Did the management emerge to be powerful than the board & shareholders? Did the board ignored compliance & governance related issues of the management which got hidden by beyond expectation performance?
Did the board & management compromise prudence & discipline for greed & rat race?

There’s bound to be failure (later if not sooner) if either the management or the board has an upper hand over the other and worse if the management stay dominant over the board!

If we go deeper on all these cases, the issues will be on the (improper) balancing play between the board & top management!

items.description_html:
RT Neelkanth Mishra
As expected, with the fiscal headwinds fading and monetary headwinds (falling credit growth till 1HFY26) becoming tailwinds (credit growth accelerating), GDP growth is surprising on the upside, and should help push up consensus trend-growth estimates to 7%-plus. That is, with a neutral fiscal and monetary policy, the economy should still register 7.5% growth.

In this light, I was shocked to see the ill-educated and egregiously wrong claims made by some that if the 'original' base of June-2025 quarter was used, growth in the June-2026 quarter would be much lower.

The new series introduced in Feb-2026 cleaned up the data and also significantly improved the methodology. For those who track this for a living (and I used to be one such till 45 days ago) - the downward revision in the base was known in March (see our note published on 1-Mar):
https://research.axiscapital.co.in/ResearchPortal/Download?E=bbebfkbdb

As our note acknowledged, the new series increased credibility of estimates of real output.

That claim is so obviously wrong that several logical rebuttals have already been made. But bad information tends to travel further than good information, and so it is important to reiterate and reinforce the argument.

That such claims got traction is itself surprising, given that easy-to-track and not-possible-to-fudge indicators of economic activity have been so robust. While June-quarter data was strong, that momentum has picked up:
- personal vehicle (cars, SUVs) dispatches grew 35% YoY in August despite just 9% growth in exports. Even two-wheeler growth is now >20% (though helped by strong exports).
- And if that was consumption, commercial vehicle dispatches grew >40%.
- tax collection growth has picked up meaningfully. This is as real as it gets.
- Credit growth continues to surprise on the upside (albeit on a low base). Last year most believed the then-weak credit growth was a demand problem, whereas we steadfastly stated it was a supply issue - it has for now been addressed.
- indicators of construction are robust.

Hopefully, now there will be fewer people asking "why private sector investment is weak," given that there is clear evidence of investments.

That said, there is still slack in the economy, as seen in weak real-wage growth. It may take several quarters of above-trend growth for that slack to tighten, and bring back sticky inflation pressures.

items.title: Moderna is up ~100% premarket after melanoma vaccine trial success. Short explainer on why stock moved 100%+ rather than 20% The vaccine is not a prev...
items.description_html:
Moderna is up ~100% premarket after melanoma vaccine trial success. Short explainer on why stock moved 100%+ rather than 20%

The vaccine is not a preventive vaccine like a COVID shot. It's made after patient already has cancer. Each dose is built individually for that patient from the mutations found in their own tumour — you sequence the tumour, find the mutated proteins unique to it ("neoantigens"), and make an mRNA shot that teaches the immune system to hunt cells carrying those specific mutations.

It's the first proof the idea works. Neoantigen vaccines have been a theoretical hope in oncology for years, but this is the first randomised Phase 3 trial designed to definitively prove the benefit.

If the mechanism is real, it's platform technology — the same pipeline could in principle be pointed at lung, kidney, bladder cancers. One analyst noted the results also read positively for the vaccine's ongoing studies in other cancer types. That optionality is what "holy grail" headlines are reaching for.

items.description_html:
4 Ways Super El Niño Could Squeeze Global Sugar Supply

El Niño could reduce exportable sugar in 4
ways:

1. Drought during the sugarcane growing season can reduce the cane yields, lowering the amount of sugarcane produced per hectare.

2. Floods during the harvest can disrupt harvesting operations and reduce the sugar content of cane, cutting sugar output even if cane volumes are strong.

3. Because corn is an important feedstock for ethanol production alongside sugarcane, a weaker corn crop due to El Niño-related droughts may divert more
sugarcane into ethanol production, leaving less sugar available for export.

4. Concerns about El Niño-related production losses may trigger precautionary export restrictions, which is likely a larger risk for global supply than the
potential crop losses themselves.

items.title: On-Demand Consumer Services: Supply Retention and Innovation as Competitive Differentiators The on-demand consumer services industry is experiencing s...
items.description_html:
On-Demand Consumer Services: Supply Retention and Innovation as Competitive Differentiators

The on-demand consumer services industry is experiencing significant evolution, with supply retention and innovation emerging as critical success factors. The founding team product lead at Pronto emphasizes that long-term success depends on supply acquisition, training, and retention, not just pricing or instant service models.

Industry Evolution and Market Dynamics

The industry is not new in terms of consumer need, but platforms are innovating on supply models through batching, microclusters, and dark stores/hubs to meet on-demand expectations. The market remains highly fragmented, with the combined market share of major players representing only 2%-3% of the total overall market, indicating significant growth potential.

Supply as the Critical Differentiator

Supply placement, training, and retention are the critical differentiators; platforms must balance these elements to meet demand and achieve high fulfillment rates. The expert notes that supply is the answer to competitive success, as without adequate supply in a particular area, platforms cannot service demand even when consumer intent exists.

Financial Sustainability Through Recurring Orders

Recurring orders (where customers book regular, repeated services) are key to achieving break-even and profitability, with a 25% recurring order mix serving as a target for financial sustainability. The business model transitions from instant and scheduled services to recurring arrangements, where customers select frequency and intervals for service delivery without discounts.

Cost Structure Evolution

Cost structure is heavily influenced by real estate, supply acquisition/retention, and logistics. Platforms are shifting from minimum guarantee to per-order payout models and reducing fixed costs via microclusters and partnerships. The industry is moving away from the minimum guarantee model toward per-order compensation, similar to the evolution seen in ride-sharing and food delivery platforms.

Non-Monetary Retention Strategies

Non-monetary retention levers are being deployed to retain supply and differentiate from competitors. These initiatives include education funding for workers' children, gold bonds, and safe hubs with childcare. Pronto specifically implements programs such as funding education for workers' children after six months of service with a 4+ rating, providing spousal employment opportunities, and establishing gold bond schemes that compound annually.

Operational Models and Geographic Expansion

Three distinct operational models have emerged among major platforms:

Urban Company operates predominantly on batching and scheduling, with only 10%-15% of their fleet open to the instant model.

Snabbit operates from the microcluster model, placing supply where demand exists in parks, small stalls, and hotels near residential areas.

Pronto operates a hybrid dark store model combined with microcluster operations, providing infrastructure for supply management while maintaining flexibility.

Geographic expansion decisions are based on household-society density, app opens and intent data, presence of quick commerce stores, area density analysis, and offline surveys.

Funding and Competitive Positioning

Pronto has raised approximately $60 million in total funding, including $50 million from the last two rounds and $13 million before that, with a $200 million valuation in the most recent $50 million round. The company's founder was 22 years old when starting the company, with a background in venture capital rather than the consumer services industry.

items.title: RT Neelkanth Mishra: As expected, with the fiscal headwinds fading and monetary headwinds (falling credit growth till 1HFY26) becoming tailwinds (cred...
items.description_html:
RT Neelkanth Mishra
As expected, with the fiscal headwinds fading and monetary headwinds (falling credit growth till 1HFY26) becoming tailwinds (credit growth accelerating), GDP growth is surprising on the upside, and should help push up consensus trend-growth estimates to 7%-plus. That is, with a neutral fiscal and monetary policy, the economy should still register 7.5% growth.

In this light, I was shocked to see the ill-educated and egregiously wrong claims made by some that if the 'original' base of June-2025 quarter was used, growth in the June-2026 quarter would be much lower.

The new series introduced in Feb-2026 cleaned up the data and also significantly improved the methodology. For those who track this for a living (and I used to be one such till 45 days ago) - the downward revision in the base was known in March (see our note published on 1-Mar):
https://research.axiscapital.co.in/ResearchPortal/Download?E=bbebfkbdb

As our note acknowledged, the new series increased credibility of estimates of real output.

That claim is so obviously wrong that several logical rebuttals have already been made. But bad information tends to travel further than good information, and so it is important to reiterate and reinforce the argument.

That such claims got traction is itself surprising, given that easy-to-track and not-possible-to-fudge indicators of economic activity have been so robust. While June-quarter data was strong, that momentum has picked up:
- personal vehicle (cars, SUVs) dispatches grew 35% YoY in August despite just 9% growth in exports. Even two-wheeler growth is now >20% (though helped by strong exports).
- And if that was consumption, commercial vehicle dispatches grew >40%.
- tax collection growth has picked up meaningfully. This is as real as it gets.
- Credit growth continues to surprise on the upside (albeit on a low base). Last year most believed the then-weak credit growth was a demand problem, whereas we steadfastly stated it was a supply issue - it has for now been addressed.
- indicators of construction are robust.

Hopefully, now there will be fewer people asking "why private sector investment is weak," given that there is clear evidence of investments.

That said, there is still slack in the economy, as seen in weak real-wage growth. It may take several quarters of above-trend growth for that slack to tighten, and bring back sticky inflation pressures.

RT Aditi Shrivastava
🚨🚨Only 15% of deeptech funds invest at TRL 1–3, when a technology is still moving from basic research to proof of concept.

This leaves a clear funding gap for investors willing to engage early.

Most deeptech capital enters only after the technology has progressed beyond the proof-of-concept stage.

About 60% of funds invest at TRL 4–6, when technologies move into demonstration and validation, while 69% invest at TRL 7–9, when they move towards deployment and commercialisation.

Biotech is particularly affected, with companies spending years on research and validation before commercialisation.

Source-IVCA
